trust_decision.summary: Each untrusted multipart part header line (up to CPPHTTPLIB_HEADER_MAX_LENGTH=8192 bytes) is matched by a recursive std::regex in FormDataParser::parse; the fix decides to recognise 'Content-Disposition: form-data;' with a linear hand-written prefix scan so that header length cannot drive libstdc++ regex recursion depth.

landing_point.why: Advisory names std::regex in multipart filename parsing; the only regex in FormDataParser::parse is re_content_disposition, and the filename* branch right below it (httplib.h:7771-7785) is the obvious first stop.

fix_sites.entry_point: Server POST/PUT/PATCH handlers receiving multipart/form-data (Request::form via Server::read_content at httplib.h:10894-10899, and ContentReader handlers via read_content_with_content_receiver at httplib.h:11352/11363), both through read_content_core httplib.h:10981-10996
same multipart route; filename*= parameter prefix check (refactor only, no regex at pinned commit)
helper start_with_case_ignore gains an offset argument; new helper parse_content_disposition (fix.diff:93-121)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Published fix touches only FormDataParser in httplib.h; no second implementation, lower-level API or wrapper is changed.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The other std::regex uses on peer-controlled data are client-side response parsing (status line, Location, WWW-Authenticate) or path/routing matching, not multipart filename parsing, so a solver can argue the advisory is about the server's multipart parser only.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Case-insensitive 'Content-Disposition:'/'form-data;' with optional spaces/tabs must still parse name/filename/filename* (incl. case-insensitive UTF-8'' prefix and long 8000-char values); a too-strict replacement breaks legitimate uploads, and over-tight length caps break the existing long-filename test.

O6_input_shapes: Content-Disposition header with mixed case name and 'form-data;' token
whitespace (spaces/tabs) after the colon and after 'form-data;'
long parameter tail near the 8192 header limit (filename*= 8000 chars)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client response status line matched by std::regex with lazy (.*?) reason capture on a line up to CPPHTTPLIB_MAX_LINE_LENGTH=32768 from the server
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: client side, response from a server the user chose to contact; not multipart
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~4300 lines from landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client redirect Location header (up to 8192 bytes) parsed by a std::regex URL pattern with unbounded ([^?#]*) / (\?[^#]*) / (?:#.*) captures
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: only reached when follow_location is enabled; client-side redirect feature, not form parsing

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Digest WWW-Authenticate / Proxy-Authenticate header iterated with std::sregex_iterator using (.+?) and "(.*?)" captures
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: only reached under CPPHTTPLIB_SSL_ENABLED with digest credentials set (httplib.h:12637-12649, httplib.h:15358); an 'unsupported combination' argument

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Static-file content-type lookup runs std::regex_search \.([a-zA-Z0-9]+)$ on the request-derived path (path up to 8192)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: mount-point/static-file feature; pattern looks simple and anchored
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~2800 lines before landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: RegexMatcher runs std::regex_match of an application-supplied route pattern over the full request path (up to 8192)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: pattern is chosen by the application author; documented behaviour (httplib.h:1550-1557)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Content-Type part header recognised by a std::regex (e.g. ^Content-Type:\s*(.*)$) instead of start_with_case_ignore
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Mirrors the existing re_content_disposition idiom in the same loop; a maintainer would naturally write both the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parse_disposition_params implemented with an sregex_iterator over key="value" pairs, like parse_www_authenticate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already uses that exact iterator idiom at httplib.h:8357-8368 for a structurally identical key=value header.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parse_multipart_boundary extracting boundary= with a regex
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Boundary extraction is a classic regex one-liner; it reads the attacker-controlled request Content-Type.

O9_family: ReDoS / uncontrolled recursion in std::regex (CWE-1333, CWE-674)

O10_build.toolchain: g++/clang with libstdc++; CMake or test/Makefile with GoogleTest
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.cc MultipartFormDataTest.* (e.g. AlternateFilenameLongValueAndCaseInsensitive at test/test.cc:11612); tests start a local Server/Client on localhost

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace only re_content_disposition with a string scan (or cap the header length) and stop, leaving the other std::regex calls on peer data untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The filename* regex was already removed by an earlier fix (commit 8bffbe3 'Merge commit from fork'); the pinned test at test/test.cc:11639 already covers a 2000-char filename* value, and this fix only raises it to 8000 (fix.diff:139-150).
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell). This is a single-header library with a large test.cc and a bundled benchmark/crow; tiny_repo (<5 MB source) is likely but unconfirmed, so it is not listed as a red flag.
Not run: whether each O8 regex actually overflows the stack at its input bound (8192/32768) under libstdc++. This is inferred from the advisory's own 8000-char trigger on a (.*) capture.
present_in_latest is unknown for all O8 routes: no latest release was provided.
All O8 routes are WHERE-type and sit in the same single file; a grep for std::regex surfaces them all, so their value as levers is weak per lessons-v2.
